title: Functoriality of the sequential derived inverse limit
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], an abelian category with enough
injectives. Fixing a functorial K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ of every
cochain complex in $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$, the assignment

$$
 \Rlim:D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))\longrightarrow D(T_{\Proet},A),
 \qquad
 M_\bullet\longmapsto\varprojlim_nI_n
$$

is a triangulated functor, and any two such choices of functorial K-injective
resolutions give isomorphic functors.

Its values are sequential derived inverse limits in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit].

(*Source note:* Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Definition (Tag
[08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)) defines the derived-limit
property by a distinguished triangle; it does not choose functorial cones.
Theorem (Tag [079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)) supplies
functorial K-injective resolutions in a Grothendieck abelian category.
Lemma (Tag [0BK7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK7)) gives existence
of derived limits for inverse systems of bounded-below derived objects.
The unbounded strict-tower triangulated functor and the natural comparison
between resolution choices asserted here require the argument below.)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ and $\mathcal B=\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)$, with the coefficient sheaf and strict towers of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use K-injectivity in the abelian category $\mathcal C$, as defined for an arbitrary abelian category by [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]; this is the Hom-complex definition of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] with $\mathcal C$ in place of the etale module category. Define $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ by the ordinary inverse limit. Its sections are compatible families of sections of the tower. Componentwise addition makes the induced map $L(f+g)=L(f)+L(g)$, and compatible families in $L(M\oplus N)$ are exactly pairs of compatible families, so $L$ is additive. Applied termwise to complexes, $L$ sends a homotopy $h$ to the homotopy $L(h)$: applying $L$ to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives the same equation. This requires a homotopy in the category of strict towers, hence one compatible with all transition maps; unrelated levelwise homotopies would not suffice.

source.place: Proof, final sentence on inverse limits of homotopy equivalences; expanded at chain level

proof.text: For a complex $M$ of towers write $u_M:M\to I(M)$ for the fixed resolution. For $\alpha:QM\to QN$ in $D(\mathcal C)$, define $\bar\alpha:I(M)\to I(N)$ in $K(\mathcal C)$ to be the unique morphism whose localization is $Q(u_N)\alpha Q(u_M)^{-1}$. This exists and is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied in the abelian category $\mathcal C$, since $I(N)$ is K-injective. Set $\Phi(\alpha)=Q_{\mathcal B}(L(\bar\alpha))$ and $\Phi(QM)=Q_{\mathcal B}(L(I(M)))$. The localization equations for identities and composites, and injectivity of the same Hom map, give $\overline{1}=1$ and $\overline{\beta\alpha}=\bar\beta\bar\alpha$. Thus these formulas give a functor. On a chain map $f:M\to N$, naturality of $u$ gives $\bar{Qf}=[I(f)]$. For a quasi-isomorphism $f$, $\bar{Qf}$ is an isomorphism in $K(\mathcal C)$, whose inverse is the unique lift of $Q(u_M)(Qf)^{-1}Q(u_N)^{-1}$; consequently $L(I(f))$ is a homotopy equivalence. The chain-level assignment therefore inverts quasi-isomorphisms and descends through the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with precisely the morphisms just constructed.

The construction in the preceding step is the K-injective construction of the unbounded right derived functor of the additive functor $L$. Apply [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] to $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$: the derived categories are those of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and K-injective resolutions in $\mathcal C$ are fixed in the hypothesis. For the target category $\mathcal B$, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies to the ringed pro-etale site with coefficient sheaf $A_T$, on the small skeleton in the larger universe fixed by [def-weil-size-convention], and supplies K-injective resolutions there. All hypotheses of the general theorem are thus met. It equips $\Phi=RL$ with natural commutation with integer shifts and shows that it sends every distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle. In particular this holds for unbounded complexes; no bounded-below computation lemma is being substituted. To make the identification with the generic construction explicit, let $w_M:M\to R(M)$ be the K-injective resolutions used for that construction. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the morphism $Q(w_M)Q(u_M)^{-1}$ lifts uniquely to $e_M:I(M)\to R(M)$ in $K(\mathcal C)$, and its inverse lifts with target $I(M)$; their composites are identities by injectivity of the Hom maps. For $\alpha:QM\to QN$, both paths in the comparison square localize to $Q(w_N)\alpha Q(u_M)^{-1}$, so they are equal by the Hom bijection with target $R(N)$. Applying $L$ and $Q_{\mathcal B}$ therefore gives a natural isomorphism from $\Phi$ to this generic $RL$. Define the shift isomorphism of $\Phi$ by composing this comparison, the shift isomorphism of $RL$, and the inverse shifted comparison. For any distinguished triangle its image under $\Phi$ is then isomorphic, including the last arrow, to its image under $RL$; it is distinguished by closure under triangle isomorphisms in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For another functorial resolution $v_M:M\to J(M)$, let $c_M:I(M)\to J(M)$ be the unique homotopy-class map with $Q(c_M)=Q(v_M)Q(u_M)^{-1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to the K-injective target $J(M)$. The inverse is the unique lift with K-injective target $I(M)$ of $Q(u_M)Q(v_M)^{-1}$. The two composites localize to identities, hence are identities in the homotopy category by injectivity. Therefore $c_M$ is a homotopy equivalence of strict towers. By step 1, $L(c_M)$ is a homotopy equivalence, so $Q_{\mathcal B}L(c_M)$ is an isomorphism. For $\alpha:QM\to QN$, the two maps $c_N\bar\alpha_I$ and $\bar\alpha_Jc_M$ have localization $Q(v_N)\alpha Q(u_M)^{-1}$. The Hom bijection with target $J(N)$ makes them equal in $K(\mathcal C)$; applying $L$ gives the naturality square in $D(\mathcal B)$. These components are consequently a natural isomorphism between the two functors, rather than merely objectwise comparisons.

Finally [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit-computation] applies to each resolution in $\mathcal C$ and identifies $Q_{\mathcal B}(\varprojlim_n I_n)$ as a representative of the sequential derived inverse limit of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. Thus the triangulated functor just constructed has the values asserted in the statement. This comparison uses the general-tower computation exactly as that cited node states it; Stacks' truncation-tower lemma alone is not being used for an arbitrary tower. The Roos-triangle definition [def-weil-derived-limit] specifies the derived-limit property of these values; it is not used to choose morphisms or to assert functoriality of unspecified cones.

split_report.summary: No new nodes. Constructed morphisms by the Hom bijection for K-injective targets, checked localization and naturality explicitly, used the closed general unbounded derived-functor theorem for triangles, and separated the general-tower Roos computation from functor construction. The statement is unchanged; K-injectivity is interpreted in the tower category, not in the etale coefficient category.
split_report.blueprint: Proof: first sentence (resolution hypothesis), middle sentence (computation and triangulatedness), final sentence (choice independence); fixes nonfunctorial cone and incompatible levelwise homotopy gaps.

tool_uses.why: Supplies K-injective resolutions for the ringed pro-etale target category to check the general derived-functor theorem; the etale-only existence statement in this unit does not do so.

statement_change.what: K-injectivity is a property of cochain complexes. Resolving only objects of the abelian tower category (placed in degree zero) does not specify the asserted unbounded functor. Replace every object by every cochain complex, as required by the original proof steps 2–4 and Stacks 079P. Make the already asserted Rlim value property cite its existing definition explicitly, following proof step 5; no boundedness, coefficient or geometric hypothesis is changed.

lean.statement: theorem sequentialDerivedInverseLimit_functorial (T : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : Scheme.AdicCoefficientDatum A) [EnoughInjectives (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d)] (I : CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ ⥤ CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ) (η : 𝟭 (CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ) ⟶ I) (hI : ∀ M : CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ, QuasiIso (η.app M) ∧ (I.obj M).IsKInjective) : ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ⥤ DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicModules T d)) (_ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF ≅ I ⋙ (lim : Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d ⥤ Scheme.CompletedAdicModules T d).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q), (∃ (_ : RF.CommShift ℤ), RF.IsTriangulated) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d), IsAdicSequentialDerivedLimit T d M (RF.obj M)) ∧ ∀ (J : CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ ⥤ CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ) (ν : 𝟭 (CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ) ⟶ J), (∀ M : CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ, QuasiIso (ν.app M) ∧ (J.obj M).IsKInjective) → ∀ (RF' : DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ⥤ DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicModules T d)), Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF' ≅ J ⋙ (lim : Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d ⥤ Scheme.CompletedAdicModules T d).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) → Nonempty (RF ≅ RF')
